title: Ordering and holding cost against order size
caption: Ordering cost 60000/Q falls with Q while holding cost 1.5Q rises. Their sum is smallest where the two are equal, at Q = 200, with each costing £300 and the total £600 a year.
alt: Three curves against order size Q: a falling ordering cost, a rising holding-cost line and their U-shaped sum with its minimum 600 at Q = 200 where the first two cross at 300.
description: Orders per year D/Q cost S each: 60000/Q.
Average stock Q/2 costs H each: 1.5Q.
The total is smallest where they cross: Q = √(2DS/H) = 200, with 6 orders a year.
At Q = 200 each cost is £300, total £600.
